title: compass-cadence-personal-okr-draft-jae-kim
content:
Quick orientation: this is my rolling, intentionally messy OKR scratchpad for Q1–Q2 2026. It's a working doc — short check-ins every Monday, a small experiment list, and a measurement ledger so I don't confuse activity for progress.

Why this format?
- I want a lightweight weekly habit (15–25 minutes) to recalibrate micro-hypotheses against measurable signals.
- Keep ideas cheap: capture, rate-limit execution, and iterate on one experiment at a time.

Current northstar (personal, product-facing): Increase the % of new Redwood API customers who integrate the SDK example and send a first inference request within 48 hours of signup ("first-call conversion").

Top-level OKR draft (lean):
- Objective: Reduce friction from signup -> first successful inference call so more teams hit the "value moment" quickly.
  - KR1: First-call conversion rate from signup -> first request within 48h: 22% -> 35% by end of Q2.
  - KR2: Median time-to-first-call: 18h -> 6h.
  - KR3: Drop-off points identified (top 3) instrumented with event tags and small follow-up nudges implemented.

Leading indicators I care about (tracked weekly):
- Weekly signups who click "SDK quickstart" (click-through %)
- % of those who open the browser-based quickstart sandbox (playground opens)
- Average steps (distinct events) completed in the quickstart flow
- Support threads started about installation / credentials (lower is better)

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Removing an explicit token copy step on the quickstart reduces time-to-first-call by ~40%.
   - Experiment: embed ephemeral token in the quickstart iframe for new signups (A/B).
   - Metric: time-to-first-call by cohort, and friction comments in support threads.
2) A small example that demonstrates a "complete feature" (e.g., simple chat message flow) leads to higher retention on first-week usage than a minimal hello-world snippet.
   - Experiment: replace the 3-line example with a 12-line chat flow in the sample repo for 25% of new signups; measure first-week active calls.
3) A single-line CLI example with prefilled prompts will convert power-users faster than SDK tutorials.
   - Experiment: surface a CLI card on the signup success page for devs who selected "CLI" during onboarding.

Current experiments (active / paused / planned):
- Active: quickstart-iframe-ephemeral-token (A/B) — owner: me; rollout: 10% -> 50%; notes: watch for token leakage edge cases, need SRE sign-off on token TTL.
- Paused: new-sample-repo-chat-flow — paused until we can add telemetry for message-send events (blocked by infra ticket JIRA-5482).
- Planned: CLI-card-surface (target start: next Monday).

Measurement plan (short):
- Define cohort = users created in the same calendar week.
- Primary signal: percent with first successful API response event within 48h.
- Secondary: median time-to-first-call, number of unique SDK installs, number of support messages mentioning "token" or "credential".
- Data sources: analytics events, support tag searches, instrumentation on quickstart page (page events).

Weekly check-in template (Monday quick ritual):
- What moved last week? (one-line)
- What metric moved? (actual numbers vs target)
- Biggest blocker?
- Small experiment to run this week (owner & success criteria)
- 2-minute reflection (what I learned)

Last three check-ins (brief):
- 2026-03-09: Moved quickstart iframe to 10% roll; first-24h cohort early signal: median time-to-first-call down 12% in A group. Blocker: token TTL race.
- 2026-03-02: Completed instrumenting quickstart clicks and sanitized event names. Observed lots of "read docs" clicks but not the final run button.
- 2026-02-23: Decided to prioritize a runnable sample over more docs; drafted chat sample but paused for telemetry gating.

Retrospective notes (what's working / what's not):
- Working: small targeted experiments (A/B) give quick signals and are easy to roll back.
- Not working: trying to run too many experiments at once dilutes instrumentation and my attention. Need to strictly cap to 1 active hypothesis at a time.

Blockers & risks:
- Infra: telemetry pipeline (JIRA-5482) must land before we can validate chat-sample hypothesis.
- Security: ephemeral tokens approach needs SRE review to confirm acceptable TTL and rotation pattern.
- Noise: organic variation (region-based signups) confounds short-window experiments — use at least 2 weeks per cohort when possible.

Action items (next 7 days):
- [ ] Follow up with Luis on telemetry ticket (JIRA-5482) — ask for ETA and fallback plan (due: 2026-03-12) — owner: Jae.
- [ ] Draft the CLI card copy and a/b mock for product to review (due: 2026-03-15) — owner: Jae.
- [ ] Put a short note in #sre about ephemeral token TTL proposal and request review (due: 2026-03-11) — owner: Jae.
- [ ] If iframe A shows >15% reduction in time-to-first-call by March 16, scale to 50% and measure support thread delta — owner: Jae.

Open questions / notes to self:
- What counts as a "successful first call" for server-side frameworks that proxy requests? Should be explicit: a 200 + inference event emitted by server.
- How to credit multi-device journeys (developer starts quickstart in browser then finishes via CLI)? Attribution rule draft: count if any of the tracked events complete within 48h and map back to initial signup id.
- Can marketing add a tiny blurb on the welcome email pointing to the runnable sample? Quick ask might move the needle cheaply.

Quick links (for later):
- Onboarding analytics dashboard (internal): https://internal/redwood/insights/onboard
- Infra ticket: JIRA-5482 (telemetry pipeline)
- Experiment doc: github.com/redwood-inference/experiments/quickstart-iframe

Closing micro-mantra: ship small, measure from the user lens, one experiment at a time.

Raw scratchpad (brain dump):
- Consider a "first-call checklist" modal that appears at signup completion for users who are flagged as "developer" — could drop friction by prefill.
- If quickstart iframe isn't feasible because of security, explore a one-click CLI flow using deep-linking into a preinstalled tool (requires product ops).
- Keep weekly digest short — ideally one bar of numbers I can scan in under 60s.

End of doc (for now).
